verdict: Serious Go SDK: clean-architecture layout (domain/usecases/infrastructure) around The Odds API v4 with concurrent bookmaker-pair/triple permutation arb detection, correct stake math, env-only credentials, tests for client and usecases, CI with CodeQL/golangci/dependabot. Badge-heavy README describing a 'professional quant pipeline' (CLV, sharp money, RLM, signal engine) that the code does not match: most src modules are 1KB stubs, requirements.txt and models/model.py are empty, main.py chains files via os.system on CSVs that must be generated first, and the only real substance is one competent betting_market_model.py doing logistic regression on hand-rolled Elo plus a simulated-odds CLV loop. Data is a 8KB nfl_games.csv and generate_test_odds.py simulation, so the CLV/sharp-money machinery runs on synthetic lines. Struct's claims are aspirational relative to implementation.
venues: simulated odds (generic the-odds-api call in utils)

verdict: University-grade microservices demo of a whole bookmaker back office: Go balance service + TypeScript bet/event/live-result services + a Rust/Rocket odds-service that computes its own Elo probabilities (no external feed), all gRPC-interconnected over Kubernetes manifests with Mongo/MySQL, an Azure Service Bus queue receiver, and a Vue/Vuetify web client with bet and balance modals. Struct confirmed exactly ('no odds integration'); the committed 18MB compiled Go binary alongside full source is a redundant build artifact, not obfuscation, so judged on source.

Single-file PyPI package (pip install oddsapi_ev) whose one function data() sweeps every sport on The Odds API across all four regions and three markets, computes EV by two fair-odds standards — vig-removed cross-book average and vig-removed Pinnacle — then filters/sorts (odds band, max vig, min EV, book count, width) into a pandas frame; JSON-file replay mode included for quota-free analysis. Struct confirmed; genuinely useful +EV screener wrapped neatly, but quota-hungry (README warns 150-350 requests per market sweep) and no backtest or staking logic.

Master's-thesis repo (Spanish-authored) on EPL betting: understat xG/npxGD, SoFIFA squad ratings + transfer budgets and football-data.co.uk odds merged into a central DB (Rmd EDA + Python feature code), a Keras neural net for 1X2 probabilities (committed .h5), then a genuine financial layer comparing Kelly (general/restricted, fractional f=0.17) vs Markowitz portfolio staking with simulated wealth curves. Struct confirmed on all three sources and the Kelly thesis; 4MB figuras.zip is transparent figure transport, and arbitrage analysis of track/take on Pinnacle vs market is included.

Large hobbyist-industrial soccer predictor: fbref + oddsportal scrapers feeding a MongoDB warehouse (with committed multi-GB .bson backups of fixtures/match_stats/odds), Poisson-xG and Elo feature builders, and a twice-fit stacked ensemble (model_stacked_2fit_* ~28KB each) predicting outcome plus home/away goals across ~15 leagues worldwide, with merge/dupe-delete tooling and actual prediction spreadsheets in made_predictions/. Struct confirmed (stacked ensemble, outcome+goals); data_sources [] understates the real fbref/oddsportal pipeline and venue none is right — predictions show odds but no staking or betting execution. Repo weight is all committed data, source itself is ~20 files.

Three-script batch pipeline for The Odds API v4: ThreadPool fetcher dumps ~46 soccer league odds JSONs to datatxt/, an Excel-maker flattens h2h outcomes per match into xlsx sheets, and a checker sums inverse max prices across the three outcomes to flag arb<100% — the whole repo is the fossil output of one September-October 2024 run (committed datatxt/, dataxlsx/ incl. a LibreOffice lock file). Struct confirmed as fetch+Excel export, 'bot' overstates it: no scheduling, key is the placeholder 'place_api_here'. Math is correct but naive — takes max price per outcome from the same sheet without verifying bookmakers/outcome alignment edge cases.

Polished NBA moneyline-inefficiency project with an honest ablation trail: feature-importance CSVs comparing leaky (edge-from-odds) vs clean team-stats models, logistic model with isotonic calibration, 7MB official bet-results simulation + equity curves, segment analysis, Snowflake warehouse load scripts, Lambda/FastAPI dashboard API and a React/Vite stakeholder/engineer frontend deployable to S3. Struct confirmed on the leakage-checks, bankroll sim and AWS/Snowflake deployment; data source is a CloudFront-hosted Kaggle-style odds dump per the README rather than a live API (no live fetch code), and .claude/launch.json shows AI-assisted development. Outputs committed make the claims verifiable offline.

Discord-posting bot that live-fetches PrizePicks' unauthenticated partner projections API (a genuinely useful keyless endpoint) but gets its 'sportsbook odds' from a hardcoded personal-path CSV (/Users/rshiknis/...) produced by some offline tool, then does EV/over-under merging on it. README's Odds API integration claim is refuted by the code — no the-odds-api call exists in picksmart_bot.py — and the repo is one 12KB script plus render screenshots. Works on exactly one Mac.

Personal The Odds API v4 arbitrage scanner with a rotating-key pool (keys.txt/spentkeys.txt bookkeeping, empty as they should be), 23-sport sweep, future-time gating, pickle-persisted opportunity objects and CSV analysis tooling, plus a launch-links.json of deep URLs into Indian/offshore books (Unibet.in, BetOnline, MyBookie, BetMGM.in) for manual two-click execution and audio alerts; committed multi-MB opportunities*.csv files prove it ran seriously in the 2021 NCAA/Euro season window. Struct confirmed as scanner; no placement automation, and ~19MB of result CSVs and .idea cruft inflate the tree.

Impressive single-file browser SPA (68KB index.html, GitHub Pages-hosted): BYO Odds API key with CORS-proxy fallbacks (allorigins/codetabs), four simultaneous de-vig engines (Pinnacle-sharp, additive, multiplicative, power) rendering true probabilities side-by-side, +EV finder, live arbitrage scanner, Kelly sizing at full/half/quarter/ten, and a local-storage bet tracker with CSV export. Struct confirmed as dashboard with real math; 'AI-powered' in the README is marketing gloss — there is no AI component in the code.

CSCI 3308 team semester project: Express/Handlebars/MySQL web app that pulls The Odds API v4 sports/odds and lets logged-in users combine book offers into 'risk-free' bet calculations, wrapped in PDFs, standup logs and 6MB of team headshots. Struct confirmed as student project, but the repo is a secret leakage clinic: live .env with Postgres creds, session secret and a real the-odds-api key ('ruan's school email api key'), the same key duplicated in backupkey.txt, and a full 4096-bit RSA private key PEM committed under background/. Core odds math is fine; everything else is coursework scaffolding.
secrets: .env: POSTGRES_PASSWORD=XXX, SESSION_SECRET, the-odds-api API_KEY XXX committed in ProjectSourceCode/.env
same the-odds-api key duplicated in background/backupkey.txt
RSA private key committed: background/csci3308safebet_key.pem (-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY----- XXX)

verdict: Railway-deployable Express MVP: three hard-coded EPL bots (match odds, over 2.5, under 2.5) pulling only bookmakers[0] from The Odds API into SQLite with a tiny dashboard. Struct confirmed as placeholder-model MVP — and worse than admitted: the over/under bots compute EV as (1/odd)*odd−1, which is identically 0, so ev>0.03 can never fire and two of the three bots are dead math; only matchOddsBot's devig-normalized comparison does anything. README itself flags probabilities as placeholders.
venues: single book (first in list) via the-odds-api

verdict: Exemplary single-file Python CLI over The Odds API v4: gitignore-style bookmaker/market filter files with regex support, automatic per-event market discovery, timezone-correct daily windows, and audit-friendly JSON outputs embedding full request meta (rate-limit state, applied rules). Struct confirmed; deliberately reads the key from a gitignored odds-api-key.txt instead of env as a design choice. Zero dependencies beyond requests, clean argparse surface (list-sports/slate/event/direct-endpoint), though single-tenant and one-day-at-a-time.

One 2022 Jupyter notebook that pulls the 'upcoming' 8-game slate from The Odds API, computes unbiased cross-book arb stakes per outcome, and writes a heavily styled openpyxl bets.xlsx — a clean, well-commented single-pass tutorial of exactly the struct description. API_KEY.txt is the literal placeholder 'PLACE API KEY HERE' (no committed secret), Books.txt is a 2022 bookmaker dump, and it only handles the first market (h2h) of each book. Dated but correct arb math.

Packaged MLB value-bet CLI: DraftKings sportsbook page scraper (keyless HTML), pybaseball team/player stats pipeline, a normal-Poisson prediction model with walk-forward evaluation, and a value calculator with edge thresholds and optional Kelly staking, wired through a tidy argparse interface (odds/stats/train/predict/value) with real unit tests and logging utils. Struct confirmed on both claimed sources; code quality is coursework-plus, but there's no evidence of historical accuracy testing in-repo (models/ is empty except .gitkeep) and the DK page-scraping is brittle by nature.

Structured NFL pipeline (collect→engineer→train→predict→visualize CLI): Odds-API v4 plus API-Sports american-football client with rate-limit base client, ~50 documented feature builders (DVOA-style, red-zone, situational), four model trainers (XGB/LGBM/RF/GB) with ensemble prediction and min-edge bet surfacing. Architecturally the most complete of this author's repos and largely runnable, but README-level stats lists several features (e.g., special-teams DVOA) the code approximates rather than sources, and the shipped .env.example contains the author's two real API keys in plaintext. Struct's sport 'basket' is a mislabel — it's NFL.

Misnamed repo ('Keiba' = horse racing in Japanese) that actually scrapes Princess Connect! Re:Dive game update-news archives into monthly CSVs and runs keyword frequency analysis — 300 committed HTML dumps of priconne game sites and zero betting, odds or racing code. Struct's screen nailed the mislabel ('not sports betting'). As a text-mining toy it functions, but relevance to the study is nil; kept only as an FP audit row.

Stdlib-only betting analytics toolkit with real unit tests per module: Poisson/Normal player-prop projection from game-log windows, Elo with home-advantage and MOV for game outcomes, vig-stripping fair probabilities, fractional-Kelly staking, 4-5 leg parlay and round-robin combinatorics ranked by combined edge, a LiveStatsFeed polling adapter, and a bet tracker reporting ROI and CLV. Struct confirmed ('CSV data, prop prediction + parlays') — honest about independence assumptions on correlated legs; the shipped data is sample-sized, so it's a framework awaiting a real feed rather than a running system. Naming (Bot365 vs 'predictive-sports-betting') suggests account churn/rebrand.

Far more than the 'Jupyter trend notebooks' the screen guessed: a full Turkish-language Next.js/Prisma/Postgres online-bookmaker platform ('Vorabahis') with auth+sessions, wallet ledger with deposit/withdraw flows (display-only, README explicitly states no processor is wired), KYC pipeline with document storage, promo codes/referrals/leaderboards, a 39-test settlement engine, admin backoffice with odds editor, and a pluggable sports-data sync over the-odds-api, football-data.org v4, ESPN, OpenLigaDB and TheSportsDB. Struct refuted (no notebooks); engineering is production-shaped with audit scripts and guard rails, and the one risk flag is a real turnkey grey-market sportsbook kit — seeded demo admin creds are in the README by design.

Idiomatic Rust CLI (tokio-free, reqwest+indicatif) that enumerates The Odds API sports, pulls h2h odds per event, picks the best price per outcome skipping exchanges (betfair_ex_au), and reports arbitrage ROI with optimal stake split behind a progress bar; committed arbitrage.json/sportsbook.json snapshots show it running against the AU Ladbrokes slate. Struct confirmed; small but complete and correct arb math, key read from .env with 8-byte template, README even leaks the author's old fork URL (k4yp). Limitations: h2h-only, no totals/spreads, no continuous mode — one-shot scan.

Node.js/Express EPL prediction engine ('preziceri' = Romanian for pricer): Dixon-Coles bivariate Poisson + Elo + form/momentum/H2H/referee stat modules fused in a weight-optimized ensemble, backtester with metrics, draw-detector, upcoming-fixtures pull from football-data.org v4, committed E0 CSVs 2005-2024 as the training corpus, and a polished Romanian-language dark-theme web UI on Vercel. Struct confirmed (Dixon-Coles + Elo on football-data.co.uk CSVs); no README in repo but scripts double as documentation, and there's no odds-comparison/value layer — it outputs probabilities, not bets.

Three files (README, app.py, home.html) for 'Footodd.io', a Heroku Flask demo: RandomForestClassifier on venue/opponent/hour/day codes plus rolling-form columns for EPL predictions, with a 70:30 EV-hedging 'strategy' described in prose. Struct's football-data.co.uk source matches the notebook-style data munging, but the referenced betting_db.csv/matches.csv/Book2.csv are not committed and the claimed the-odds-api historical database has no ingestion code or endpoint in app.py at all — the repo cannot run as-is. Candid README admits low model confidence; UI is a stock Webflow template.
venues: bet365/bwin/pinnacle etc (odds columns from absent CSV)

verdict: Disciplined XGBoost match-winner pipeline over a full vendored clone of Jeff Sackmann's tennis_atp corpus (1968-2024 singles/challenger/futures/doubles CSVs committed): prepare script enforces strict time-based train (1991-2021) / validation (2022) / test (2023-24) splits with explicit no-post-match-leakage feature construction, Optuna tuning, calibration variants and JSON reports with prediction CSVs. Struct confirmed as tennisabstract-lineage XGBoost (source attribution and CC BY-NC-SA license respected). Practical caveat: prediction-only — no odds, no market comparison, and the multi-hundred-MB dataset fork is the bulk of the repo.

Real two-sport production-ish platform: FastAPI backend with Alembic migrations, Postgres/Redis, alert engines that compare XGBoost predictions to the-odds-api prices and push value/CLV alerts to Telegram, football models (outcome/goals/corners HT-FT pickles committed) plus a tennis vertical built on Sackmann CSVs pulled from GitHub raw with four total-games model generations and a 2MB tennis SQL dump, RapidAPI api-football and open-meteo weather as auxiliary features, React dashboard on Railway. Struct's 'xgboost.readthedocs.io' data_source is a screen artifact — actual sources are richer; the many apply_*_fix.py one-offs and test2.html show rapid personal iteration. Telegram bot token stays in env.
venues: telegram alerts; multi-book via odds api

verdict: Unusual and well-built: a Claude Code/Codex agent-skill (21KB SKILL.md) for Chinese 竞彩 football betting that ships two stdlib-only Python tools — a defensive fetcher for Sporttery's public webapi (with browser headers, per-pool error isolation and computed sales-cutoff windows) and an odds-math CLI for implied/no-vig probabilities and EV — plus explicit anti-hype rules distinguishing 'like the pick' from 'the odds have value'. Struct confirmed; the fetch_sporttery.py endpoint is a genuinely keyless source for Chinese lottery lines that almost no other repo touches. It is prompt-pack + tooling, not an autonomous bot.

Operationally serious single-repo soccer system: modular train/backtest/analyze/quality-gate pipeline over five top-league football-data CSV snapshots, calibrated result+OU models, walk-forward backtests with enforced temporal guards ('train before test, odds as-of'), rolling strategy/threshold policy stores, and a providers layer spanning football-data.org v4, the-odds-api, SofaScore api/v1, flashscore and a Betburger-style GraphQL odds host (global.ds.lsapp.eu). Struct confirmed incl. policy learning; 12 pytest modules and pre-upload hygiene checks; committed config.local.json is env-placeholder-only (clean), and public Google-Sheet results tracking adds claimed verifiability. Main smell: three 90-130KB monolithic *_module.py files.

Small, correct, continuously-running two-way arbitrage scanner for The Odds API US moneylines: per-sport polling intervals via SPORT_CONFIGS env, best-price-per-outcome comparison, exact stake-split and ROI math in utils, slippage cutoff that skips games starting within N minutes, and append-only arbitrage.csv logging. Struct confirmed; notable care for its size (env-driven config, timeout+raise_for_status, clean separation) — but only handles exactly-2-outcome h2h markets and silently keeps scanning draws games via the len!=2 filter even where 'continue' was commented out in the slippage branch.

Clean, genuinely functional FastMCP stdio server over the Matchbook betting-exchange REST API: httpx async client with paginated event search (back-lay, decimal, price-depth params), session auto-login from local .env with token kept memory-only, and seven tools including matchbook_place_lay that places real lay bets plus offer status/cancel — the rare MCP wrapper with true write-side betting capability. Struct confirmed; README's honesty (unofficial, 'real money, always confirm', representative-transcript disclosure) and SECURITY.md discipline are above corpus norm. Read-only-ish on money: no withdrawal/payment surface.

NFL 2024 moneyline predictor: scripted pipeline (Data Scraper for nfl-data_py-style raw CSVs, offensive/defensive averaging features, one-hot encoding) training Logistic Regression, Random Forest and Gradient Boosting, with prediction CSVs committed and a React+CRA front consuming a local Flask /api/matchups endpoint to render weekly matchup cards with three-model confidence bars. Struct confirmed as model+web-UI with no external data_sources listed (correct: no odds API at all — moneyline is just the win label); a ~20MB committed dataset makes it reproducible but the ML is basic means-history with no leakage analysis or backtest.

Two standalone RandomForest scripts over committed historical CSVs (7 years of UCL from football-data.co.uk-format exports plus an EPL archive) that compute last-5-game form/attack/defence features and emit probability CSVs, deliberately oriented to 'safe bets': Over 1.5 bankers, refundable Asian lines (Over 2.0), and double chance when a straight win is shaky. Struct confirmed (RF + historical-csv, venue none); the safety-first market selection is a coherent opinion rather than EV math, no odds comparison happens anywhere, and one script's team-name map is hardcoded league-specific.

Self-declared prototype betting assistant: the-odds-api h2h fetch + keyless statsapi standings/scores + rotowire injury scrape + openai 'advisor' wired into a tkinter watchlist loop, but the README honestly lists most subsystems as planned/not-functional and the code confirms it — mlb_run_assistant.py has mangled indentation (functions defined inside dead main()) and an enrich path stuffed with hardcoded demo odds (spread -5.5, ML +160/-190, 'news_headlines': [...]). Struct's underdog.com integration does not exist in any file, and sportradar trial stats endpoint sits in a module the run loop barely uses.
venues: us books via odds api (injury/underdog legs absent)

verdict: Modern async live-arbitrage discrepancy monitor: Playwright+Camoufox (anti-fingerprint) scrapers as a BaseScraper strategy pair for Bet365.es In-Play and Winamax.es live markets, injecting JS match selectors to pull per-match odds, then normalizing team names through a manual/auto mapping store and cross-comparing paired live matches on a local HTTP dashboard with manual /api/link matchmaking. Struct confirmed (both books, live discrepancies, async); architecture is genuinely clean (structlog, pydantic, ruff, pytest-asyncio) and the 'next_goal' market selectors show real in-play betting depth; winamax.fr in struct is actually winamax.es.

Selenium bot automating the Bac Bo casino dice game on a bettilt mirror: reads the live scoreboard, applies pattern-triggered bets with up to 2-step 'gale' (martingale doubling) escalation, and pushes emoji/sticker alerts to a Telegram channel with a daily restart loop and Dockerfile. Struct confirmed as bot/casino — but this is online-casino bet placement, not sports betting: the strategy is negative-EV martingale on an RNG game, login creds go through env (placeholders in repo), and the registration affiliate links were scrubbed to example.com. Real code that really clicks bet buttons; no sportsbook anywhere.

Betflow: a genuine data-engineering capstone deployed on AWS — Airflow DAGs (ingestion+DQC, batch glue jobs, dbt staging/marts), Kafka producer orchestration with retry/health handlers, Spark streaming transforms, Snowflake with SQS/SNS notifications, and a dbt layer whose marts are betting-specific (fct_betting_value, fct_market_efficiency, fct_odds_movement, bookmaker performance) fed by the-odds-api (live+historical), ESPN live scoreboard, api-sports per-league APIs, weather (open-meteo/openweathermap) and RSS/news connectors; showcase'd by Zach Wilson. Struct confirmed on the Airflow/dbt/Snowflake stack; the 'sportsbook' data source means API feeds, and the README candidly explains why dashboards stay private (arbitrage legal + cost). Caveat: pipeline runs can't be reproduced without the author's AWS, and producer_config keys are dev placeholders, not secrets.

NBA underdog value study (2009+) with a full scraping→feature→model-selection pipeline: betexplorer match-odds scraper plus patched basketball-reference widget scrapers merged into per-season master frames (rolling win pct, player availability/star-impact proxies), then GridSearchCV logistic regression, SVM and forest/GBT ensembles with ROI tests and a written final report PDF. Struct confirmed on both keyless sources and the LogReg+SVM claim; the repo bloats itself with hundreds of committed per-fold .pkl models (~698 files) and a stray extensionless 'logistic_regression_function' file, and the pipeline is a one-off research run, not an operative tool.

Small, thoughtful line-shopping collector: argparse CLI fetches one sport/region/market from The Odds API (credit headers tracked), flattens event→bookmakers→markets→outcomes into a timestamped SQLite table, and report.py runs SQL for best price per side, inter-book disagreement and per-event line movement/trend. Struct confirmed; stands out for a demo mode (bundled sample_data.json, zero-key pipeline) and a README 'what I learned' section documenting real metric bugs (American-odds gaps meaningless on lopsided games → measure disagreement in implied-probability space). h2h-only, single-machine, no scheduling — a foundations project, competently done.

Arbitrage alert pipeline with a keyless heart: a Playwright OddsPortal scraper (~35 league listing URLs, parallel match pages, min-5-bookmaker filter) engineered as a drop-in replacement for The Odds API, feeding 2-way/3-way arb math with stake splits, Discord alerts (incl. a delayed 'free alerts' queue) and a GitHub Actions cron. Struct confirmed on the mechanics but the real source is oddsportal.com scraping, and there's an undisclosed commercial layer: marketing.py auto-posts digests to Bluesky and drafts blog content via the Anthropic API for an 'ArbFactory' Discord funnel (ko-fi link included). Rounding unit-tested; book-URL obfuscation in test_rounding.py suggests ToS-sensitivity.

Genuine small JavaScript client wrapper for the paid JsonOdds API: builds https://jsonodds.com/api/<endpoint> requests with a JsonOdds-API-Key header supplied by the user at construction. Confirms struct 'api-wrapper for sportsbook odds'; the API fronts Pinnacle/Bookmaker/BetOnline/Bovada/GTBets feeds. No key committed (the README UUID is an example eventId, not a token).
confirmed: JS wrapper over jsonodds.com with API-key header auth

verdict: Student soccer-prediction project: Jupyter notebooks (dataset prep, feature selection via BorutaPy, RF/GB models, a 'Betting Simulation' notebook) over manually-downloaded football-data.co.uk CSVs plus 8 data splits. Confirms struct 'model/notebooks'; refutes any tooling angle - no odds API, no live data pipeline, everything offline CSV. Includes 44MB of committed data dirs.
confirmed: notebook ML pipeline with betting simulation
refuted: real_tool as reusable tooling - it is offline study notebooks

verdict: Working Python CLI bot that logs into kicktipp.de (German fantasy tipster community), fetches matchday odds pages and auto-submits score predictions before the deadline via a login cookie token, with pluggable predictor modules. Confirms struct 'bot/kicktipp.de' exactly; note kicktipp is free-to-play fantasy, not a wagering sportsbook. Token is user-supplied at CLI, nothing committed.
confirmed: automated bet placement with login-token auth

verdict: Well-organized end-to-end NBA value-betting system: nba_api data fetch, rolling-feature XGBoost classifier, honest backtest module, value_finder comparing model prob to implied odds from The Odds API, SQLite P&L tracker, Streamlit dashboard, optional Claude agent that degrades gracefully. Confirms struct 'model + the-odds-api' with real betting logic (Kelly sizing present). Keys only in .env.example placeholders; nothing committed.

Single R script + README describing 'ALICE', an XGBoost college-football spread model built on cfbscrapR/cfbfastR (CollegeFootballData) loads and hand-computed game-level features. Struct 'model' confirmed; the packet's sport='book' mislabels it (it is CFB, venue none). API key is an obvious fake placeholder string committed in code.
confirmed: XGBoost CFB spread model in R
refuted: live sportsbook data source - uses historical CFB data APIs

verdict: HKJC horse-racing prediction study: Selenium crawlers scraping racing.hkjc.com racecards/results/odds pages plus MLP/CNN/LSTM/SVM modeling in Keras, with ~60MB of committed dataset CSVs. Struct confirmed; dated code (keras.wrappers, sklearn.externals) so effectively archived. No keys; HKJC pages are public HTML.

Real MCP server (FastMCP, PyPI-published) exposing 12 tools that proxy a commercial backend API at sportsbettingaianalyzer.com via X-API-Key header: /api/picks/*, /api/stats/*, /api/analyze, /api/health. Struct confirmed; caveat is the backend is the author's own paid service and win-rate claims (59-60%) are self-reported, unverifiable from this repo. Key is env-var only.
confirmed: MCP wrapper over an odds/picks API with auth

verdict: Real but abandoned (README says so) Python bot that scrapes Cloudbet sports-api v6 events and Thunderpick /api/markets, computes cross-book arbitrage, and actually places LTC-denominated bets via Cloudbet place-bet and Thunderpick wager endpoints. Struct confirmed strongly (venue=sportsbook, cloudbet+thunderpick). A live-looking Thunderpick session token was committed in source.
secrets: thunderpick token XXX committed in ThunderpickBetManager.py
confirmed: crypto-arb bot placing real bets on two books

verdict: Scala.js + Python hybrid app: a Scala/AJAX odds viewer plus Scala crawler modules (Sherdog, Bookmaker.eu lines) and a Node/npm-fronted 'historical betting analyzer'. Struct confirmed 'scanner/odds analysis'; endpoints are sparse because most URLs live in vendored node_modules/package-lock noise — the real ones are lines.bookmaker.eu and a sherdog.com crawl. Academic-leaning, mixed build, functional core.
confirmed: scrapes bookmaker.eu lines + sherdog MMA stats

verdict: Genuinely rigorous NBA player-props research repo: LightGBM mean+dispersion models with leak-free rolling features, injury-report parsing, live Odds API quotes (DK/FanDuel/BetMGM/BetRivers), pre-registered holdout, forward paper-trading ledger, and a day-by-day JOURNAL. Struct confirmed; it self-reports 'no proven edge' (-1.8% holdout ROI), which is exactly the honest framing the quality-4 screen implies.
confirmed: LightGBM props model + leak-free features + ledger
uses the-odds-api and NBA injury feed
refuted: any claim of a live profitable edge - authors themselves refute it

verdict: Full-stack PrizePicks companion: Flask backend with logistic-regression over/under models built on nba_api/statsdmz data plus a scraper against app.prizepicks.com (committed past_lines dumps), and a create-react-app frontend (its package-lock accounts for the 1300+ npmjs URL hits). Struct confirmed model/nba.com; it is more app than research. No keys committed.
confirmed: LR model + Flask/React app for PrizePicks O/U
refuted: venue linkage - it targets a DFS app not a sportsbook

verdict: Clean three-notebook football pipeline (exploration, calibrated modelling, market simulation with flat/fractional-Kelly staking and ROI/Sharpe/drawdown evaluation) over football-data.co.uk CSVs, with committed output JSON summaries. Struct 'model + calibration + Kelly' confirmed precisely; UUID hits are just nbformat cell IDs, not secrets. No live API code.

Real sharp-money detector: Node collector polls TxLINE (txline.txodds.com /odds/updates, guest JWT via unauthenticated POST /auth/guest/start) into SQLite, detect.js fires on >=2.81pp/5min pre-match moves calibrated from 8.46M harvested ticks with Brier validation, and results are served keyless via REST/MCP/x402 pay-per-call plus Telegram alerts. Confirms struct 'scanner/txodds/sharp money' and the REST/MCP/x402 claim exactly; backtest honestly labels n=18 as suggestive.
confirmed: served via REST/MCP/x402 with no key

verdict: Two analysis notebooks extending Stern (1994)'s time+lead win-probability formula with pregaming spreads, using static Kaggle CSVs (nba odds, 1949-2024 results) and play-by-play data from a third-party dataset. Struct 'model' confirmed; academic exercise, not tooling - no code fetches data live and no betting loop. UUID hits are notebook cell IDs.

Real FastAPI+React monorepo football forecaster: Postgres/alembic backend with Poisson services (estimate_lambdas, over/BTTS probs), edge/EV pricing, grading, paper-bet routes, and seed scripts that pull api.football-data.org/v4 fixtures and api.the-odds-api.com/v4 odds; deployed at football-forecaster.onrender.com with heavy AI-generated docs. Struct 'model + paper betting app' confirmed (venue none is fair - it aggregates book prices for value, never places bets).
confirmed: Poisson model + EV/edge pricing + paper betting ledger

verdict: Single 430KB portfolio notebook: live NFL spread lines from The Odds API v4 (75 games cited) vs 35 years of Kaggle spreadspoke history, computing juice/hold and binomial tests of favorites/rest/scheduling inefficiencies. Struct confirmed; the author openly frames it as a job-portfolio piece. API key is a YOUR_API_KEY_HERE placeholder.

Student capstone: Kaggle NBA/EPL notebooks (RF, LR, XGBoost, sequential) plus an AWS Lex chatbot folder; README conflates AWS Chatbot/cost-anomaly docs, suggesting boilerplate padding. No training on real market data, Windows-machine-bound, and the 2-line README oversells it. Struct 'model/multi' — scraping yes, model no.
